# AGENT_ZERO_CONTROL_PLANE_TOKENS every mutation is rejected while reads stay open.
# Comma-separated name:token bearer credentials.
AGENT_ZERO_CONTROL_PLANE_TOKENS=
# Comma-separated repository paths tasks.create may target.
AGENT_ZERO_CONTROL_PLANE_REPOSITORIES=
# Comma-separated name:mode|mode execution-mode grants. Without a grant a principal may only
# request the non-writable observe and suggest modes.
AGENT_ZERO_CONTROL_PLANE_MODES=
# Comma-separated origins allowed to read /api/v1/** cross-origin via CORS. Empty by default:
# tasks.list/tasks.get/health are unauthenticated by design, so letting a browser read their
# responses from another origin is an explicit opt-in, not the default.
AGENT_ZERO_CONTROL_PLANE_ORIGINS=
# Authentication (apps/dashboard/server/auth.config.ts), mounted in-process at /api/auth/**.
# Use the NUXT_-prefixed name: the module requires it in production and only falls back to
# BETTER_AUTH_SECRET in development.
NUXT_BETTER_AUTH_SECRET=
# Dashboard (apps/dashboard), the single deployable app: UI, oRPC/OpenAPI routes, and
# authentication all share one origin (default port 3000, override with PORT). Sign-in
# capabilities are derived from AUTH_ENABLE_SIGNUP and the GitHub OAuth credentials above at
# build time, so rebuild whenever those policy values change. NUXT_PUBLIC_SITE_URL is optional:
# the auth module auto-detects the base URL from the incoming request, and this only needs to be
# set for a custom domain or deterministic OAuth callbacks.
NUXT_PUBLIC_SITE_URL=

standalone instance factory (`createAuth`) for callers that own their own secret and origin. No
HTTP server, no runtime imports.

runtime, GitHub, models, and config packages; nothing composes into it, and it does not depend on

`/api/v1/**` (OpenAPI), plus `GET /api/dashboard`, and mounts Better Auth in-process at

only component with a database credential. See the `orpc-server` skill.

`control-plane.ts`, `access.ts`, and `dashboard.ts`. `packages/api` holds no HTTP host of its
own — it only exports `rpcRouter`, `requestLoggerStorage`, and the plain functions those depend
on. It does not depend on `packages/auth`.
- The HTTP host is Nuxt's own Nitro server. Routes live in `apps/dashboard/server/`:
- `routes/rpc/[...].ts` mounts `rpcRouter` over `RPCHandler` (the typed RPC transport).
- `api/v1/[...].ts` mounts the same `rpcRouter` over `OpenAPIHandler` (REST + docs at `/api/v1/docs`).
- `auth.config.ts` (at the `server/` root) configures `@onmax/nuxt-better-auth`, which mounts
`/api/auth/**` itself — there is no hand-written auth route file.
- `api/dashboard.get.ts` serves the aggregate dashboard view.
Both `server/**/*.ts` and `app/**/*.ts` use explicit imports rather than Nuxt's auto-imports:
`apps/dashboard/tsconfig.json`'s plain `tsc` pass (part of `typecheck`, separate from `vue-tsc`)
has no visibility into Nuxt's generated ambient auto-import types.
- `apps/dashboard` pins `nuxt` to the stable v4 channel (`^4.5.2` in `package.json`), whose
`@nuxt/nitro-server` depends on `nitropack` v2 + classic h3 (`h3@^1.15.11`, also a direct
dependency), not the standalone Nitro v3 package. Route handlers use classic h3's API:
`import { defineEventHandler, toWebRequest } from 'h3';`. Call `toWebRequest(event)` to get a
standard `Request`, pass it to `handler.handle(request, {...})`, and return the resulting
`Response`. Do not reach for Nitro v3's Fetch-first `defineHandler`/`EventHandlerWithFetch` from
`nitro`/`nitro/h3`; that API belongs to the unreleased `nuxt-nightly` v5 channel this project does
not use.
- Declare a procedure's HTTP method, path, tags, and summary with `.meta(openapi({...}))`
(`import { openapi } from '@orpc/openapi'`), not the `.route({...})` sugar from
`@orpc/openapi/extensions/route`. That extension patches `.route()` onto the builder via a bare
side-effect import; Nitro's production bundler tree-shakes it away even though the package's own
`sideEffects` field marks the module as one to keep, silently dropping every `/api/v1/**` route
while `/rpc/**` and the build both still look fine. `.meta(openapi(...))` is a real import a
bundler can't discard, and is what `.route()` expands to internally. This metadata only affects
the OpenAPI transport; the RPC transport ignores it. Add it whenever a procedure should be
reachable over `/api/v1/**`, which today means every procedure.
`apps/dashboard/server/utils/store.ts`, so KV drivers stay interchangeable; never store review
input or checkout paths. ViteHub is composed into Nuxt's own Nitro build by the local
`apps/dashboard/modules/vitehub.ts` Nuxt module (calling `vite-hub/nuxt`'s undocumented
`viteHubNuxtModule(options, nuxt)` export directly — there is no `modules: ['vite-hub/nuxt']`
one-liner). Prove KV changes with a real `nuxt build` and a request against a route that reads
the store, not just `nuxt prepare` or a type check.
- Nuxt's Nitro server is the only top-level HTTP host; do not introduce Express, Hono, or a second
one.

+// imports `@agent-zero/mail`, which keeps one capability package from depending on another.

## Summary - Extract the control-plane API into a dedicated `packages/api` package with an oRPC router, control-plane operations, and Better Auth app composition - Add an OpenAPI/REST transport at `/api/v1/**` with auto-generated docs at `/api/v1/docs`, alongside the existing typed `/rpc/**` oRPC transport - Consolidate Better Auth and the API layer to run in-process inside `apps/dashboard` (same-origin, SSR-enabled), removing the standalone `apps/auth-server` and `apps/server` apps entirely - Compose ViteHub's KV Runtime Helper into Nuxt's own Nitro pipeline via `apps/dashboard/modules/vitehub.ts` - Add request logging to the oRPC router ## Why The control plane previously spanned three separate deployables (`apps/server`, `apps/auth-server`, `apps/dashboard`) with cross-origin auth and duplicated CORS/transport wiring. Moving the API surface into `packages/api` gives `apps/dashboard` a single, typed composition point for the runtime, GitHub, models, config, and auth adapters — matching the `packages/api`/`apps/dashboard` boundary described in `CLAUDE.md`. Hosting auth in-process and enabling SSR removes distributed configuration complexity and allows server-side session access for hydration. `apps/dashboard` is now the only component that owns a persistence layer, reached exclusively through the auth adapter's own instance, keeping `packages/auth` free of HTTP/runtime imports as required by the architecture boundaries. ## Verification - [x] `aube run check:repo` - [x] `aube run lint:ci` - [x] `aube run typecheck` - [x] `aube test` - [x] `aube run build` All commands pass locally against the full monorepo. ## Safety and compatibility - [x] I added or updated deterministic tests for changed behavior. - [x] I preserved `observe` mode as read-only, or explained the policy change above. - [x] Runtime commands and target-repository writes remain inside the runner boundary. - [x] I did not expose secrets, tokens, personal data, or untrusted output in logs. - [x] I updated documentation and Agent Skills when workflows or boundaries changed. ## Reviewer notes This branch spans three commits building up the restructuring: 1. `ef51721` — extract the API layer into `packages/api` with OpenAPI support 2. `60ee356` — consolidate auth and API in-process in `apps/dashboard` 3. `76a8e48` — remove the now-unused `apps/server` app entirely and wire up ViteHub inside Nuxt's own Nitro build `apps/auth-server` and `apps/server` are fully removed; `apps/dashboard` is now the single deployable app and the only component that owns a persistence layer. --- Need help on this PR?
